resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Both runs agree: no braille anywhere near this citing location (braille.lines: []) — this is the suggested wording embedded inline in rule 17.11.1d's own running text (source lines 13686-13688), not a worked example with its own braille page. illustrates.rule already carries this quote's own genuine rule id in both runs ('17.11.1d'), NOT a shared placeholder — unlike the §19 gold precedent's own six embedded 'Sample:' files, this section's two embedded quotes have no placeholder-id defect to fix.
